Notes the missing timeout and retry or idempotency handling on the charge call. Gives concrete restructured code: short transactions, the charge outside any transaction with an idempotency key and a timeout, a conditional final transition (only from the pending state), and emails via a queue. States the recovery path for a crash between the charge and the final write (a reconciler re-driving stuck pending orders with the same idempotency key, or the provider's webhook as the source of truth). Every finding has an estimated impact, a 'Breaks at' point, and a verification step.
expectations: Reports the transaction held open across the charge call and email sends as the top finding, rated critical or high
Uses Little's Law: 150 req/s times the charge latency against 80 pooled connections (20 x 4 pods)
Notes the 5-second default timeout of Prisma's interactive transaction, which can roll back after the card was charged
Flags the unbounded Promise.all email fan-out and moves it to a job enqueued after commit
Restructures the code: charge outside any transaction with an idempotency key and timeout, then a conditional transition from pending

evals.expected_output: Flags the cache key missing the org id as the top finding: one org's dashboard is served to every other org, which is a data leak and a correctness bug, not just a performance issue. It is critical, with a pointer to the security review skill. Notes the stampede: when the hot key expires every 5 minutes, all concurrent landing-page requests for that org run the ~3 s aggregate at once, with an estimate tied to login traffic. Mitigations are request coalescing or a short lock, stale-while-revalidate, or TTL jitter. Also raises at least one of: no invalidation when the underlying data changes (the TTL is the only plan), unvalidated `range` letting clients create unbounded keys, and behavior when Redis is slow or down (client timeout, fallback). Recommends asking whether the 3 s aggregate itself should be fixed, since the miss path stays slow. Verdict: Block.
expectations: Reports the cache key missing the org id as the top finding: one org's dashboard is served to other orgs
Rates it critical and points to the security review skill
Explains the stampede when the hot key expires and offers coalescing, a short lock, stale-while-revalidate, or TTL jitter
Raises at least one of: no invalidation on writes, unvalidated range creating unbounded keys, or behavior when Redis is slow or down
Asks whether the 3-second aggregate itself should be fixed
Verdict is Block
